Live Map: Track the path of Hurricane Polo

2026-09-22 PBS NewsHour / Associated Press Hurricane Polo, live map, Category 5, Pacific hurricane, Mexico, National Hurricane Center, NOAA, El Niño, storm tracking, interactive map
Read the source article

Quick summary

PBS NewsHour featured a live interactive map tracking Hurricane Polo, one of the most powerful Pacific cyclones in decades, which reached Category 5 with 180 mph sustained winds and threatened Mexico's southwestern coast.

Key takeaways

  • Hurricane Polo grew into a Category 5 storm with maximum sustained winds of 180 mph (290 kph), confirmed by a NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft
  • Polo was the third Category 5 hurricane of the Pacific season, following Genevieve and Lowell
  • The storm was centered 210 miles south of Zihuatanejo, Mexico, and was nearly stationary at midday, expected to move west-northwestward
  • Polo reached speeds comparable to only a few hurricanes in recent decades, primarily Hurricane Patricia (215 mph in 2015)
  • Scientists attributed the rapid intensification to the El Niño weather phenomenon, which has fueled warmer waters and favorable wind patterns in the Pacific
  • The U.S. Embassy in Mexico issued a weather alert warning of life-threatening flooding, mudslides, and dangerous rip currents even without direct landfall
